method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18, the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05, and the writing-l4-rules skill (with references/regulative.md); the s 9 three years and the s 55 twenty-one days are regulative rules (PARTY ... DO ... WITHIN ... HENCE FULFILLED LEST PARTY ... MAY), asserted through EVALTRACE; the seat questions take plain facts; no REFUSE (gaps answer `not covered`, asserted); every opinion or satisfaction of an assessor or the District Court asked as an input; date arithmetic in one small module; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Criminal Injuries Compensation Act 2003 (WA), compilation on the Western Australian Legislation website (law_a6998, mrdoc_47649), compilation table ending with the Criminal Law (Mental Impairment) Act 2023 (No. 10 of 2023, in operation 1 September 2024), retrieved 2026-09-07, as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/mrdoc_47649.txt. No regulation amending the s 31 Table is deposited or noted in the compilation (s 31(3)); the Criminal Injuries Compensation Regulations are not deposited.

seat: the victim: the person injured by an offence; and, where the victim died, the close relative who suffered loss from the death (for whom the deceased's personal representative applies)

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run cica-dates.l4 ; l4 run cica-victim.l4 ; l4 run cica-cases-victim.l4
checks.result: 152 assertions written, 152 satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings; 2 #TRACEs as their expect lines say (2026-11-07)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. A residual DEONTIC cannot be compared with EQUALS on this l4, so the s 9 and s 55 rules are asserted through CONSIDER EVALTRACE ... WHEN FULFILLED, and one residual of each is #TRACEd.

scope: In: s 3 (injury, victim, satisfied, personal representative, proved and alleged offence, interested person, as used); s 4(1) (s 4(2) borrowed); s 6 (personal item, loss; s 6(1)(g) answered `not covered`); s 5 (as a gloss on 'convicted'); s 8; s 9(1), (2); s 10; s 11; ss 12-17 (who may apply and under which section; s 13(5), 15(5), 16(5), 17(5) folded into the assessor's satisfaction, an input); s 20(2)(d); s 23(2)-(4); ss 26, 27; s 30 (as the just amount, an input); ss 31-34; s 35; ss 36-41; s 42(2)-(5); s 43; s 47; s 48(1), (2); s 55(1), (3), (4); s 57; s 68; s 19(5), 63(5), 64(5) (natural person), 70(2), (3), 71. Out: machinery (ss 1, 2, 7, 8A, Part 8, s 72, s 73, Schedules 1 and 2); the assessor's procedural powers (ss 18, 19(1)-(4), 20(1), (2)(a)-(c), (3) save as folded into the just amount, 21, 22, 24, 25, 62A, 63(1)-(4), (6)-(8), 64(1)-(4)); s 28; s 29; s 44; s 45 and Part 6 (recovery from the offender); ss 46, 54, 69; ss 56-58; ss 65-67.
